transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (CSM), Jonas Meyer (SE), Samira Patel (Support) — Sophie Ellis (Head of ML, Winterfold), Marcus Lee (Platform), Tina Alvarez (InfoSec), Daniel Park (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Kickoff / handoff to implementation: reviewed playbook, pilot scope and success criteria.
- Discussed networking (VPC peering), security (KMS, audit logs), and deployment options (Dedicated vs Private).
- Agreed next steps: share runbook, schedule pilot, deliver benchmark harness and security artifacts.

Topics: onboarding playbook, pilot scope, networking/VPC, SOC2/KMS, cost/latency targets, benchmarks, rollout plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood. we wanted to do a quick handoff, a little bit of an onboarding playbook walkthrough and then agree pilot next steps. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Sophie Ellis: good thanks, uh yeah excited to get rolling. we've got Marcus and Tina on as well to cover infra and security.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: hey, yeah from platform side we just wanna make sure network stuff won't be a blocker, we're running in GCP in us-central1.
[00:19] Tina Alvarez: hi all, from security I'll mainly focus on encryption, KMS, audit logs, and least privilege.
[00:24] Alex Chen: perfect, i'll hand over to Priya to run the playbook items, and Jonas will do the technical bits after.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: thanks Alex. quick overview — our onboarding playbook is three phases: pilot (2–4 weeks), stabilization (1–2 sprints) and rollout. For the pilot we usually scope a narrow set of routes, e.g., inference for internal support chat and a small batch of production traffic. Success = latency p95 under 150ms for the short prompts and cost within the target range you set.
[00:54] Sophie Ellis: that's reasonable, our initial SLA for the feature is 200ms p95 but we'd like to see if we can get to 120–150 once tuned.
[01:03] Jonas Meyer: cool. for the pilot we'd recommend starting on Redwood Hosted for speed to value and then decide Dedicated or Private depending on traffic and data policy. note though, if you need VPC and customer managed KMS from day one, we'd look at Redwood Private.
[01:18] Marcus Lee: can you clarify the VPC peering flow? we prefer peering for security but want minimal ops. what does the handoff look like?
[01:25] Samira Patel: sure — we have a VPC peering checklist we send, it's mostly IAM, firewall rules, routing table entries, and a short handshake for AWS/GCP. for Private deployments there's an extra step for the control plane connectivity. we'll link the checklist.
[01:39] Tina Alvarez: and what about encryption at rest/ in transit and KMS integration? we need HSM-backed keys for certain data classes.
[01:45] Jonas Meyer: we support KMS and HSM integrations; for the pilot we usually do envelope encryption with your KMS, and we can map the key hierarchy; for HSM-backed keys we will need some paperwork and additional provisioning — i'll put that in the doc.
[01:59] Sophie Ellis: okay good. also curious about data retention—can you keep logs for 90 days and then purge? we need auditability for 90 days.
[02:06] Priya Kapoor: yes we can configure retention and export of audit logs to your SIEM. defaults vary by plan but we can draft a retention policy for you.
[02:13] Daniel Park: about rate limiting — we have bursty traffic, how would Redwood handle autoscaling and burst capacity?
[02:20] Jonas Meyer: Redwood Dedicated has predictable throughput and burst capacity options. for Hosted, autoscaling is handled in the control plane; we'll set quotas per route and can throttle gracefully. for the pilot we can simulate bursts with the benchmark harness.
[02:34] Sophie Ellis: benchmarks — can you show typical latency/cost tradeoffs and what knobs we'll be tuning?
[02:39] Alex Chen: yes jonas will share a sample benchmark harness. key levers are batching, KV cache (sorry sometimes transcriber writes KV cash), sequence length trimming, and model quantization profiles. we'll recommend a profile given your average prompt length.
[02:55] Jonas Meyer: small note — your agent prompts are short, median token length ~28 so we can be aggressive on batching without hurting SLOs. for cost-sensitive workloads we can suggest 4-bit quantization on compatible models and a batching window of 20–50ms.
[03:11] Marcus Lee: do you have any specific infra reqs for the benchmark harness? we run CI runners and can spin up a staging namespace.
[03:18] Jonas Meyer: the harness is a small python tool that hits your route; it needs a service account with token scoped to the pilot API key, and a runner with network access. i'll give the repo link.
[03:27] Priya Kapoor: action items we'll capture — Alex will share the playbook and runbook, Jonas will share the harness and recommended profiles, Samira will open the VPC peering checklist, and i'll schedule the pilot kickoff.
[03:39] Tina Alvarez: on compliance artifacts, do you have SOC2 report and diagram of data flow?
[03:44] Samira Patel: yes we have a SOC2 snapshot and a standard data flow diagram. i'll attach both; for more detailed audits we can coordinate an NDA or secure drop.
[03:55] Sophie Ellis: excellent. one more question — if during pilot we see model quality regressions after quantization, what's the rollback story?
[04:02] Jonas Meyer: we always keep a non-quantized variant available and use traffic splitting for canary. rollbacks are immediate via the console or API; if quality regresses we can fallback to the verified model. will document the rollback play.
[04:15] Marcus Lee: speaking of console, do we get token-level cost breakdowns? we need per-route cost attribution for internal chargeback.
[04:21] Alex Chen: yes console shows token-level costs, per-route dashboards, and you can export granular billing for your finance team.
[04:28] Daniel Park: timeline — when can we start pilot? we have internal readiness the week of 8/25.
[04:34] Priya Kapoor: perfect — i'll schedule the kickoff for Tues 8/26 and block 45 minutes.
[04:39] Sophie Ellis: agreed. stakeholders for kickoff: Sophie, Marcus, Tina, Daniel + Alex, Jonas, Priya.
[04:46] Alex Chen: great. any blockers on Redwood side?
[04:49] Jonas Meyer: none technical — i'll need their service account and a short list of routes to enable.
[04:55] Sophie Ellis: we'll send that by friday 8/22.
[05:00] Tina Alvarez: and we'll attach the data classification doc — need to confirm which prompts contain PII.
[05:06] Alex Chen: noted. we'll treat PII specially and can set up redaction or X-filtering as needed.
[05:11] Sophie Ellis: one small ask — we sometimes route to third-party tools during inference, any concerns with that?
[05:17] Jonas Meyer: you can call external tools via function-calling or webhooks; we recommend minimal outbound endpoints and an allowlist; we'll document patterns.
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: okay to recap — Pilot scope: 2 weeks, narrow routes (internal support chat), success: p95 <=150ms and cost target TBD. Deliverables: onboarding playbook, runbook, VPC checklist, SOC2 + KMS docs, benchmark harness, quantization recommendation. Next meeting: pilot kickoff 2025-08-26.
[05:46] Sophie Ellis: sounds good. financial question quick — do you have an estimate of pilot cost?
[05:50] Alex Chen: we'll provide an estimate based on expected tokens per day; for a small pilot usually under $1,200 for two weeks on Hosted, varies if Dedicated or Private. we'll send a pro-forma.
[06:03] Marcus Lee: last thing — are there any known competitors we should be aware of from a feature standpoint?
[06:07] Alex Chen: some customers evaluate OpenAI and Anthropic for base models; our differentiation is the serving runtime and the rollout/observability.
[06:17] Tina Alvarez: okay thanks.
[06:19] Alex Chen: anything else?
[06:21] Sophie Ellis: not on my side. excited to get started.
[06:25] Alex Chen: great. we'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar invite. thanks everyone.

End of call.
